text: Dead flies rising up [in] the ointment of a perfumer give a stench; a little folly is heavier than wisdom and honor.
The heart of a wise one [is] to his right, and the heart of a fool to his left.
And even in a fool walking along the way, his heart is lacking, and he shows to everyone [that] he [is] a fool.
If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, you should not leave your station, for calmness puts to rest great sins.
There is an evil I have seen under the sun, as an error that goes forth from before the face of the ruler:
He has set a fool in many high places, and the rich ones sit in the lowly place.
I have seen slaves on horses, and princes walking like slaves on the earth.
The one digging a pit will fall into it; and one breaking through a wall, a snake will bite him.
The one pulling out stones will be hurt by them; the one splitting trees endangers himself by them.
If the iron has been blunt, and he has not sharpened the edge, then he must exert strength; and wisdom [is] an advantage to being successful.
If the snake bites without a charm, then there is no advantage for the master of the tongue.
The words of the mouth of a wise one [are] favor, and the lips of a fool will swallow him up—
the beginning of the words of his mouth [is] folly, and the end of his mouth [is] evil madness.
And the fool multiplies words. Man does not know what will come to be, and of what will come to be after him, who can declare [it] to him?
The toil of fools wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.
Woe to you, O land, that your king is a youth, and your princes feast in the morning!
Blessed [are] you, O land, that your king [is] a son of nobles, and your princes feast in due season—for strength and not for drunkenness!
By laziness, the rafter is made to sink, and by idleness of hands, the house leaks.
Bread is made for laughter, and wine makes life merry—and the silver is the answer to all.

Even in your thought you must not belittle the king, and in the chambers of your bed do not belittle the rich, for a bird of the heavens may carry along your voice, and a possessor of wings may declare the word.
